newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PBL said buying Showboat casino stake.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PBL said buying Showboat casino stake.

text.p: Australia's richest man, Kerry Packer, plans to make a bid to buy the 26.1 percent stake in Sydney Harbour Casino Ltd held by Showboat Inc, Australian Broadcasting Corp (ABC) radio reported on Monday.
A spokesman for Packer's media group, Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd (PBL), said PBL would make an announcement to the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) today.
New South Wales Gaming minister Richard Face said an announcement by the U.S.-based Showboat and Packer's PBL would made this morning, the ABC reported.
Face said the bid requires approval by a number of organisations as well as the Casino Control Authority.
The minister said there would be probity checks of the organisations and individuals involved and those checks would be thorough.
Packer, a well known patron of casinos, has an interest in Crown Ltd, which operates the Melbourne casino.
"The announcement by Showboat and PBL is essentially a commercial arrangement which will require approval of a number of organisations before it comes to finality," Face said.

"The arrangements would also be subject to approval by the Casino Control Authority, which is under my administration, being satisfied with the relevant legal agreements and the probity organisations and individuals involved in the arrangements," he said. Showboat has a management contract to operate the Sydney casino, which is due to open a A$1 billion permanment facility later this year.

A Packer-led consortium lost out in a bid for the 12-year Sydney casino licence when it was awarded in December 1994 and his interests have launched several legal actions against the current Sydney casino owners and management.

Packer's private company, Consolidated Press Holdings Ltd, holds 50 million Crown shares or about 10 percent of the Melbourne casino operator. It also owns about 20 percent of Hudson Conway Ltd, which owns 37 percent of Crown.
Sydney Harbour Casino shares closed six cents higher at A$1.93 on Friday. PBL shares were steady at A$6.10.
